title: Training
summary: Full training with densification, SSIM, spherical harmonics and exposure correction

blocks.text:
The full training run on all images. Compared with the minimal loop in notebook 05, I added five things:

| # | Ingredient | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Densification** (MCMC strategy) | Grows the number of Gaussians from ~52k SfM points to hundreds of thousands, putting them where detail is missing |
| 2 | **L1 + SSIM loss** | SSIM rewards correct *structure* (edges, texture), not just correct average colour |
| 3 | **Spherical harmonics up to degree 3** | View-dependent colour (shine), switched on gradually |
| 4 | **Exposure compensation** | Absorbs per-frame brightness changes (see notebook 01), so they don't turn into coloured floaters |
| 5 | **Learning-rate schedule** | Big steps early, tiny steps at the end, for fine convergence |

The output is `work/splats/splats.ply`, plus checkpoints and a fly-through video. The training cell saves checkpoints and can resume after an interruption. I restart the kernel of notebook 05 first, so its GPU memory is free.

import json, math, time
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import pycolmap
from gsplat import rasterization, MCMCStrategy, export_splats
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
from IPython.display import display, Video
from PIL import Image

pycolmap.logging.minloglevel = 2
device = "cuda"
torch.manual_seed(0); np.random.seed(0)

PROJECT_DIR = Path.cwd()
DATASET_DIR = PROJECT_DIR / "work" / "dataset"     # input  (notebook 04)
OUT_DIR = PROJECT_DIR / "work" / "splats"          # output
OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
print(f"GPU: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}, {free / 2**30:.2f} GB free of {total / 2**30:.2f} GB")
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650, 2.36 GB free of 3.63 GB

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `DOWNSCALE` | 2 | Train at ½ resolution (≈1000 × 550). `1` = full resolution: sharper, but ~3× slower and more memory |
| `STEPS` | 30 000 | Training iterations. Quality still improves noticeably up to ~30k |
| `CAP_MAX` | 600 000 | Maximum number of Gaussians. **The main memory and speed knob** |
| `SH_DEGREE` | 3 | View-dependent colour detail (0 = flat colour) |
| `TEST_EVERY` | 8 | Every 8th image is held out for honest evaluation |
| `EXPOSURE_COMPENSATION` | True | Learn a brightness/colour correction per image |

Memory and run time depend mostly on `DOWNSCALE` and `CAP_MAX`. With these values my 4 GB card peaked at about 900 MB, so memory wasn't the limit; time was. A card with more memory has room for full resolution or a higher cap. If training runs out of memory, lowering `CAP_MAX` is the first thing to try, then raising `DOWNSCALE`.

QUICK = False                     # True: a short run to check everything works

DOWNSCALE = 2
STEPS = 7_000 if QUICK else 30_000
CAP_MAX = 300_000 if QUICK else 600_000
SH_DEGREE = 3
TEST_EVERY = 8
EXPOSURE_COMPENSATION = True

PREVIEW_EVERY = 500               # update the live preview every N steps
EVAL_EVERY = 2_500                # compute test-set PSNR every N steps
CHECKPOINT_EVERY = 5_000          # save a resumable checkpoint every N steps
RESUME = True                     # continue from the latest checkpoint if one exists

## Loading the dataset

As in notebook 05, but with all images. They stay on the CPU as 8-bit integers (about 300 MB of RAM), and only the one needed at each step is copied to the GPU. As floats on the GPU they would take about 1.2 GB.

rec = pycolmap.Reconstruction(DATASET_DIR / "sparse" / "0")
cam = rec.cameras[next(iter(rec.cameras))]
assert cam.model_name == "PINHOLE", "Run notebook 04 first (undistorted dataset needed)"
names = sorted(im.name for im in rec.images.values())

W, H = cam.width // DOWNSCALE, cam.height // DOWNSCALE
sx, sy = W / cam.width, H / cam.height
K = torch.tensor([[cam.focal_length_x * sx, 0, cam.principal_point_x * sx],
                  [0, cam.focal_length_y * sy, cam.principal_point_y * sy],
                  [0, 0, 1]], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

viewmats, images = [], []
for name in names:
    im = rec.find_image_with_name(name)
    vm = torch.eye(4)
    vm[:3, :] = torch.tensor(im.cam_from_world().matrix(), dtype=torch.float32)
    viewmats.append(vm)
    rgb = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(str(DATASET_DIR / "images" / name)), cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    images.append(torch.from_numpy(cv2.resize(rgb, (W, H), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)))
viewmats = torch.stack(viewmats).to(device)       # [N_images, 4, 4] world-to-camera
images = torch.stack(images).pin_memory()         # [N_images, H, W, 3] uint8, CPU (pinned = faster copies)

test_idx = np.arange(0, len(names), TEST_EVERY)
train_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(names)), test_idx)
print(f"{len(train_idx)} training + {len(test_idx)} test images at {W}×{H}  (images: {images.numel() / 2**20:.0f} MB in RAM)")

def get_image(i):
    return images[i].to(device, non_blocking=True).float() / 255
169 training + 25 test images at 1008×549  (images: 307 MB in RAM)

## What's added

### Densification

The SfM cloud is sparse: no points on smooth surfaces, few in hard-to-match areas. Training has to add Gaussians where they're needed and get rid of useless ones. gsplat has two strategies for this:

| | **Adaptive Density Control** (original 3DGS, `DefaultStrategy`) | **3DGS-MCMC** (`MCMCStrategy`, used here) |
|---|---|---|
| How it grows | Every 100 steps: **clone** small Gaussians and **split** large ones whose screen-space position gradient is high ("this area is still wrong") | Every 100 steps: add **5 % more** Gaussians, sampled where existing ones are most opaque |
| How it prunes | Delete nearly transparent or huge Gaussians. Every 3000 steps, reset all opacities | "Dead" Gaussians (opacity < 0.005) are **relocated** onto live ones instead of deleted |
| Count over time | Can **explode** unpredictably (millions) | Grows smoothly up to a **hard cap** (`CAP_MAX`) |
| Extra trick | | Adds small random **noise** to the positions of transparent Gaussians, which helps them explore the scene |

I used MCMC because its memory is predictable: `CAP_MAX` sets the budget, and the scene can't grow past it. It also needs two small regularisation terms that keep Gaussians from becoming larger or more opaque than necessary.

### Initialisation

As in notebook 05, but in the MCMC style: opacity 0.5, scale 0.1 × neighbour distance, random rotations, and zero higher-order SH, since view-dependent colour is learned later.

C0 = 0.28209479177387814                       # SH degree-0 constant: colour = 0.5 + C0 * sh0

points = np.array([p.xyz for p in rec.points3D.values()], dtype=np.float32)
point_rgb = np.array([p.color for p in rec.points3D.values()], dtype=np.float32) / 255
dist, _ = cKDTree(points).query(points, k=4)
neighbour_dist = np.sqrt((dist[:, 1:] ** 2).mean(axis=1)).clip(1e-4).astype(np.float32)

centers = np.array([rec.find_image_with_name(n).projection_center() for n in names])
scene_scale = float(1.1 * np.linalg.norm(centers - centers.mean(axis=0), axis=1).max())

def init_params(n=None):
    # Gaussians from the SfM points. If n is given (resuming), create n placeholder Gaussians instead.
    if n is None:
        n = len(points)
        values = {
            "means": torch.tensor(points),
            "scales": torch.log(torch.tensor(neighbour_dist * 0.1)).unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, 3),
            "quats": F.normalize(torch.randn(n, 4), dim=-1),
            "opacities": torch.logit(torch.full((n,), 0.5)),
            "sh0": torch.tensor((point_rgb - 0.5) / C0).unsqueeze(1),
            "shN": torch.zeros(n, (SH_DEGREE + 1) ** 2 - 1, 3),
        }
    else:
        values = {"means": torch.zeros(n, 3), "scales": torch.zeros(n, 3), "quats": torch.zeros(n, 4),
                  "opacities": torch.zeros(n), "sh0": torch.zeros(n, 1, 3),
                  "shN": torch.zeros(n, (SH_DEGREE + 1) ** 2 - 1, 3)}
    return torch.nn.ParameterDict({k: torch.nn.Parameter(v.to(device)) for k, v in values.items()})

print(f"{len(points):,} initial Gaussians, scene scale {scene_scale:.2f}")
52,425 initial Gaussians, scene scale 5.59

### Loss: L1 + SSIM

L1 compares pixels one by one, and blur changes most pixels only slightly, so a blurry render can still have a small L1 error. SSIM (structural similarity) compares local patterns in 11 × 11 windows: mean brightness, contrast, and how pixels vary together, which is exactly what blur destroys. 3DGS uses `loss = 0.8 · L1 + 0.2 · (1 − SSIM)`. My implementation, and a comparison on one photo:

def ssim(a, b, window=11, sigma=1.5):
    # SSIM between two images [H, W, 3] in [0, 1], using a Gaussian-weighted window.
    a, b = a.permute(2, 0, 1)[None], b.permute(2, 0, 1)[None]
    g = torch.exp(-(torch.arange(window, device=a.device) - window // 2) ** 2 / (2 * sigma ** 2))
    g = g / g.sum()
    kernel = (g[:, None] * g[None, :])[None, None].repeat(3, 1, 1, 1)
    blur = lambda x: F.conv2d(x, kernel, padding=window // 2, groups=3)
    mu_a, mu_b = blur(a), blur(b)
    var_a, var_b = blur(a * a) - mu_a ** 2, blur(b * b) - mu_b ** 2
    cov = blur(a * b) - mu_a * mu_b
    c1, c2 = 0.01 ** 2, 0.03 ** 2
    return (((2 * mu_a * mu_b + c1) * (2 * cov + c2)) / ((mu_a ** 2 + mu_b ** 2 + c1) * (var_a + var_b + c2))).mean()

photo = get_image(int(train_idx[len(train_idx) // 2]))
blurred = torch.tensor(cv2.GaussianBlur(photo.cpu().numpy(), (0, 0), 2.0), device=device)
brighter = (photo * 1.1).clamp(0, 1)
for label, img in [("slightly blurred", blurred), ("10 % brighter", brighter)]:
    print(f"{label:<17} L1 = {(img - photo).abs().mean():.4f}   1 − SSIM = {1 - ssim(img, photo):.4f}")

slightly blurred  L1 = 0.0091   1 − SSIM = 0.0783
10 % brighter     L1 = 0.0413   1 − SSIM = 0.0073

The blurred image has a smaller L1 error than the brighter one, so L1 alone would prefer the blur. SSIM penalises the blur about 10× more than the brightness change.

### Exposure compensation

Brightness swings noticeably between frames of my video (notebook 01). Part of that is content, but the Auto Lighting Optimizer also adjusted brightness and contrast frame by frame. Without help, the trainer would explain those changes with the scene itself, by putting darker or brighter Gaussians in front of some cameras: floaters.

So every training image gets 6 extra numbers, a gain and an offset per colour channel, and the render is corrected (`render · gain + offset`) before it's compared with the photo. The Gaussians learn one consistent exposure, and each image's deviation goes into its own 6 numbers. The final model and the `.ply` are rendered without any correction.

The corrections need an anchor. "Every image a bit darker, every Gaussian a bit brighter" gives exactly the same training renders, so the corrections and the scene can drift together. In my first full run (still with the whole video) the average gain slid to about 0.90 (0.93 / 0.90 / 0.88 for R/G/B), the model came out about 8 % too bright and slightly blue, and test PSNR was 26.5 dB even though the geometry was fine. The fix is one line: after every update, re-centre the corrections so their average over the training images is exactly no change (gain 1, offset 0). The scene then has to carry the average exposure itself.

### Learning rates

As in notebook 05, with two changes: `shN` learns 20× slower than the base colour, and the position learning rate decays exponentially to 1 % of its start value by the end.

## Training

Each step picks a random training image and renders it, with the SH degree going up by one every 1000 steps (0 → 3), so colour is learned before view-dependence. The render gets that image's exposure correction, the loss is 0.8 · L1 + 0.2 · (1 − SSIM) plus the small MCMC regularisers on opacity and scale, and after the update the strategy grows and relocates Gaussians.

The preview shows a held-out test view next to its photo. Checkpoints go to `work/splats/checkpoints/`; with `RESUME = True`, re-running the cell continues from the latest one.

CKPT_DIR = OUT_DIR / "checkpoints"
CKPT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

def make_optimizers(params):
    lrs = {"means": 1.6e-4 * scene_scale, "scales": 5e-3, "quats": 1e-3,
           "opacities": 5e-2, "sh0": 2.5e-3, "shN": 2.5e-3 / 20}
    return {k: torch.optim.Adam([{"params": params[k], "lr": lr, "name": k}], eps=1e-15) for k, lr in lrs.items()}

def render(params, viewmat, sh_degree, width=W, height=H, Ks=None):
    colors = torch.cat([params["sh0"], params["shN"]], dim=1)
    img, alpha, info = rasterization(
        params["means"], params["quats"], torch.exp(params["scales"]), torch.sigmoid(params["opacities"]),
        colors, viewmat[None], (K if Ks is None else Ks)[None], width, height,
        sh_degree=sh_degree, packed=False)
    return img[0], info

def psnr(a, b):
    return (-10 * torch.log10(((a - b) ** 2).mean())).item()

def evaluate(params, sh_degree):
    # Mean PSNR and SSIM over the held-out test images (no exposure correction).
    psnrs, ssims = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in test_idx:
            r = render(params, viewmats[i], sh_degree)[0].clamp(0, 1)
            gt = get_image(i)
            psnrs.append(psnr(r, gt)); ssims.append(ssim(r, gt).item())
    return float(np.mean(psnrs)), float(np.mean(ssims))

# --- build everything (fresh, or from the latest checkpoint) ---
checkpoints = sorted(CKPT_DIR.glob("ckpt_*.pt"))
if RESUME and checkpoints:
    ckpt = torch.load(checkpoints[-1], map_location=device, weights_only=False)
    params = init_params(n=ckpt["params"]["means"].shape[0])
    params.load_state_dict(ckpt["params"])
    optimizers = make_optimizers(params)
    for k, o in optimizers.items():
        o.load_state_dict(ckpt["optimizers"][k])
    start_step, history = ckpt["step"] + 1, ckpt["history"]
    print(f"Resuming from {checkpoints[-1].name} (step {ckpt['step']}, {len(params['means']):,} Gaussians)")
else:
    params, optimizers, start_step, history = init_params(), None, 0, {"step": [], "loss": [], "n": [], "test": []}
    optimizers = make_optimizers(params)
    print("Starting a fresh training run")

means_scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ExponentialLR(optimizers["means"], gamma=0.01 ** (1.0 / STEPS))
import warnings
with warnings.catch_warnings():                     # fast-forward the schedule when resuming
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
    for _ in range(start_step):
        means_scheduler.step()

strategy = MCMCStrategy(cap_max=CAP_MAX, refine_start_iter=500,
                        refine_stop_iter=int(STEPS * 0.8), refine_every=100)
strategy.check_sanity(params, optimizers)
strategy_state = strategy.initialize_state()

exposure = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(len(names), 2, 3, device=device))   # per image: [log-gain, offset] × RGB
exposure_optimizer = torch.optim.Adam([exposure], lr=1e-3)
if RESUME and checkpoints:
    exposure.data.copy_(ckpt["exposure"]); exposure_optimizer.load_state_dict(ckpt["exposure_optimizer"])
    strategy_state = ckpt.get("strategy_state", strategy_state)
    del ckpt
Resuming from ckpt_029999.pt (step 29999, 600,000 Gaussians)

def save_checkpoint(step):
    path = CKPT_DIR / f"ckpt_{step:06d}.pt"
    torch.save({"step": step, "params": params.state_dict(),
                "optimizers": {k: o.state_dict() for k, o in optimizers.items()},
                "exposure": exposure.detach(), "exposure_optimizer": exposure_optimizer.state_dict(),
                "strategy_state": strategy_state, "history": history}, path)
    for old in sorted(CKPT_DIR.glob("ckpt_*.pt"))[:-2]:      # keep the two newest
        old.unlink()
    return path

preview_i = int(test_idx[len(test_idx) // 2])
preview_handle = display(Image.new("RGB", (2 * W, H)), display_id=True)
status_handle = display("starting…", display_id=True)

torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
t0, step = time.time(), start_step
try:
    for step in range(start_step, STEPS):
        i = int(np.random.choice(train_idx))
        gt = get_image(i)
        sh_degree = min(step // 1000, SH_DEGREE)

        img, info = render(params, viewmats[i], sh_degree)
        if EXPOSURE_COMPENSATION:
            img = img * torch.exp(exposure[i, 0]) + exposure[i, 1]

        l1 = (img - gt).abs().mean()
        loss = (0.8 * l1 + 0.2 * (1 - ssim(img, gt))
                + 0.01 * torch.sigmoid(params["opacities"]).mean()        # MCMC regularisers
                + 0.01 * torch.exp(params["scales"]).mean())

        strategy.step_pre_backward(params, optimizers, strategy_state, step, info)
        loss.backward()
        for opt in optimizers.values():
            opt.step(); opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        exposure_optimizer.step(); exposure_optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        with torch.no_grad():                       # anchor: average correction over training images = none
            exposure[train_idx] -= exposure[train_idx].mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        means_scheduler.step()
        strategy.step_post_backward(params, optimizers, strategy_state, step, info,
                                    lr=means_scheduler.get_last_lr()[0])

        if step % 100 == 0:
            history["step"].append(step); history["loss"].append(loss.item()); history["n"].append(len(params["means"]))
        if step % EVAL_EVERY == 0 or step == STEPS - 1:
            history["test"].append((step, *evaluate(params, sh_degree)))
        if step % PREVIEW_EVERY == 0 or step == STEPS - 1:
            with torch.no_grad():
                r = render(params, viewmats[preview_i], sh_degree)[0].clamp(0, 1)
            pair = torch.cat([get_image(preview_i), r], dim=1).cpu().numpy()
            preview_handle.update(Image.fromarray((pair * 255).astype(np.uint8)))
            done = step + 1 - start_step
            rate = done / (time.time() - t0)
            last = history["test"][-1] if history["test"] else (0, float("nan"), float("nan"))
            status_handle.update(
                f"step {step + 1:,}/{STEPS:,} | {len(params['means']):,} Gaussians | loss {loss.item():.4f} | "
                f"test PSNR {last[1]:.2f} dB (at step {last[0]:,}) | {rate:.1f} steps/s | "
                f"~{(STEPS - step - 1) / rate / 60:.0f} min left | GPU peak {torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 2**20:.0f} MB")
        if (step + 1) % CHECKPOINT_EVERY == 0:
            save_checkpoint(step)
except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
    print(f"out of GPU memory at step {step}: lower CAP_MAX or raise DOWNSCALE, then re-run "
          f"(RESUME=True continues from the last checkpoint)")
    raise
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print(f"interrupted at step {step}, saving a checkpoint")
    save_checkpoint(step)
    raise

final_ckpt = save_checkpoint(step)
print(f"training finished: {len(params['means']):,} Gaussians, {(time.time() - t0) / 60:.1f} min, checkpoint {final_ckpt.name}")
starting…
training finished: 600,000 Gaussians, 0.0 min, checkpoint ckpt_030000.pt
## How it went

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 4))
axes[0].plot(history["step"], history["loss"], lw=0.7)
axes[0].set_title("training loss"); axes[0].set_xlabel("step"); axes[0].set_yscale("log")
axes[1].plot(history["step"], np.array(history["n"]) / 1000)
axes[1].set_title("number of Gaussians (thousands)"); axes[1].set_xlabel("step")
test = np.array(history["test"])
axes[2].plot(test[:, 0], test[:, 1], "o-")
axes[2].set_title("test PSNR (dB) — images never trained on"); axes[2].set_xlabel("step")
for ax in axes: ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

final_psnr, final_ssim = evaluate(params, SH_DEGREE)
print(f"final test PSNR {final_psnr:.2f} dB, SSIM {final_ssim:.3f} on {len(test_idx)} held-out images")
final test PSNR 28.30 dB, SSIM 0.900 on 25 held-out images

Gaussians grow by 5 % every 100 steps until they reach `CAP_MAX`, or until 80 % of training, when growth stops. Test PSNR climbs quickly and then flattens.

Renders next to photos for a few test views:

show = test_idx[np.linspace(0, len(test_idx) - 1, 4).astype(int)]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(show), 2, figsize=(16, 4.3 * len(show)))
with torch.no_grad():
    for row, i in zip(axes, show):
        r = render(params, viewmats[i], SH_DEGREE)[0].clamp(0, 1)
        gt = get_image(i)
        row[0].imshow(gt.cpu().numpy()); row[0].set_title(f"photo {names[i]}")
        row[1].imshow(r.cpu().numpy()); row[1].set_title(f"render — PSNR {psnr(r, gt):.1f} dB")
        for ax in row: ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

### Learned exposure

The gain per training image, in time order. Without the correction, these variations would have ended up in the scene.

gains = torch.exp(exposure[:, 0]).mean(dim=1).detach().cpu().numpy()
plt.figure(figsize=(15, 3))
plt.plot(train_idx, gains[train_idx], ".-", lw=0.8)
plt.axhline(1, c="gray", ls=":")
plt.xlabel("image (time order)"); plt.ylabel("learned gain"); plt.title("Per-image exposure correction (1 = no change)")
plt.show()
print(f"gain range: {gains[train_idx].min():.2f} … {gains[train_idx].max():.2f}")
gain range: 0.88 … 1.24

### Size and opacity

Most Gaussians should be small and either fairly opaque or almost invisible. Very large ones are often floaters, which notebook 07 cleans up.

with torch.no_grad():
    sizes = torch.exp(params["scales"]).max(dim=1).values.cpu().numpy()
    opac = torch.sigmoid(params["opacities"]).cpu().numpy()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 3.5))
axes[0].hist(np.log10(sizes / scene_scale), bins=100); axes[0].set_xlabel("log10(largest axis / scene scale)")
axes[0].set_title("Gaussian size")
axes[1].hist(opac, bins=100); axes[1].set_xlabel("opacity"); axes[1].set_title("Gaussian opacity")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

## Fly-through

The scene rendered along the original camera path, interpolated smoothly between cameras. Floaters and holes show up quickly in motion. The video is saved to `work/splats/flythrough.mp4`.

from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation, Slerp

def interpolate_path(viewmats, frames_per_camera=4, stride=3):
    # Smooth path through every `stride`-th camera: positions linearly, rotations with SLERP.
    cams = viewmats[::stride].cpu().numpy()
    c2w = np.linalg.inv(cams)
    rots = Rotation.from_matrix(c2w[:, :3, :3])
    t = np.arange(len(cams))
    ts = np.linspace(0, len(cams) - 1, (len(cams) - 1) * frames_per_camera + 1)
    rot_i = Slerp(t, rots)(ts).as_matrix()
    pos_i = np.stack([np.interp(ts, t, c2w[:, k, 3]) for k in range(3)], axis=1)
    out = np.tile(np.eye(4), (len(ts), 1, 1))
    out[:, :3, :3], out[:, :3, 3] = rot_i, pos_i
    return torch.tensor(np.linalg.inv(out), dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

path = interpolate_path(viewmats)
video_path = OUT_DIR / "flythrough.mp4"
writer = cv2.VideoWriter(str(video_path), cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"mp4v"), 30, (W - W % 2, H - H % 2))
with torch.no_grad():
    for vm in path:
        frame = render(params, vm, SH_DEGREE)[0].clamp(0, 1).cpu().numpy()
        writer.write(cv2.cvtColor((frame[: H - H % 2, : W - W % 2] * 255).astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR))
writer.release()

# OpenCV's 'mp4v' codec doesn't play in most browsers. If ffmpeg is installed, re-encode to H.264.
import shutil, subprocess
if shutil.which("ffmpeg"):
    h264_path = OUT_DIR / "flythrough_h264.mp4"
    subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-i", str(video_path), "-c:v", "libx264",
                    "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-crf", "20", str(h264_path)], check=True)
    h264_path.replace(video_path)

## Saving the model as `.ply`

`.ply` is the usual exchange format for Gaussian splats. gsplat's `export_splats` writes the layout of the original 3DGS code: position, base colour (`f_dc_*`), view-dependent colour (`f_rest_*`), opacity as a logit, scales as logs, and the rotation quaternion. That's the same form the parameters are stored in during training, so nothing needs converting.

This is the raw model, still in COLMAP's coordinate system and with floaters. Notebook 07 cleans it up for Blender and Unity. The file can already be dropped into [SuperSplat](https://superspl.at/editor) for a first look.

with torch.no_grad():
    finite = torch.ones(len(params["means"]), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    for k, v in params.items():
        finite &= torch.isfinite(v.reshape(len(v), -1)).all(dim=1)
    print(f"non-finite Gaussians removed: {(~finite).sum().item()}")
    ply_path = OUT_DIR / "splats.ply"
    export_splats(
        means=params["means"][finite], scales=params["scales"][finite], quats=params["quats"][finite],
        opacities=params["opacities"][finite], sh0=params["sh0"][finite], shN=params["shN"][finite],
        format="ply", save_to=str(ply_path))
print(f"{ply_path.relative_to(PROJECT_DIR)}: {finite.sum().item():,} Gaussians, {ply_path.stat().st_size / 2**20:.0f} MB")

## Result

600,000 Gaussians after 30,000 steps, with a test PSNR of 28.3 dB and an SSIM of 0.90 on 25 held-out images. The learned exposure gains range from 0.88 to 1.24. The raw model is in `work/splats/splats.ply`.
